column4: Summary
An editor introduced a newly unearthed memoir written by one scientific family over three generations.
A cousin arrived at their late father's manor as a sceptic and came away convinced that he had been a genius.
The spectre of war haunted the village as Separatists and Monarchists clashed near the Town Hall.
The cousins attended a lively council meeting at the Town Hall to learn the mindset of the locals.
A relieved official agreed to prepare the materials and make an announcement.
A local farmer struck up a conversation about the economy and invited a cousin to his plantation.
A young man in a brown sack suit who shared an interest in science dined with a cousin at a local cafe.
A cousin spent hours charming the locals who frequented political meetings.
A conversation with a vagrant caused a stir among the local gossips.
On an April morning the military officers asked the family to support building a barracks in town.
The family's vote on the barracks was received by the town with mild acceptance.
The victorious forces pushed the battlefront away from the village and took command of the local government.
Driven from the estate after the barracks became a target of the war, a cousin wrote from exile.
Life settled into a routine of distant gunfire by day and explosions lighting the sky by night.
Separatist soldiers interrogated the returning family and kept watch over the town from a new outpost.
A cousin was rewarded for the family's contributions and political allegiance, with more promised for supporting the war.
A cousin offered the military schematics for advanced weaponry in exchange for further investment.
A cousin tested new weapons on the estate, attracting attention for better or worse.
One faction criticised the cousin's weapons while the other was keen to curry favour.
The Monarchy insisted on military service to quell the uprising, or a penalty in its place.
A militia lieutenant asked the family to house the leadership of an overcrowded encampment.
The military repeated its demand for quarters, this time with the assistance of guns.
Busy with internal matters, the military could not enforce the quartering edict and moved on.
With ingredients scarce in wartime, a cousin decided to simply attach guns to everything.
A well-placed bribe and some showmanship impressed the military.
The military mocked a cousin's plan to combine weaponry with more weaponry.
After a dreadful royal tea party, a cousin plotted with the family to burn down a Monarchist building.
The cousins' combined talents turned a target into rubble, inspiring the townsfolk.
The cousins decided against sabotage, and the afternoon tea incident went unavenged.
Those who had contributed to the war effort could switch sides before the end.
With its buildings destroyed, the faction that had controlled the town limped away in defeat.
The resistance failed, and the controlling faction kept its grip on the town.
The family's financial pledges decided which army could supply its troops and win the war.
The cousins' advanced weaponry proved decisive on the battlefield.
Feeling ignored and spited, a cousin considered sabotaging a faction's building or a member of their own family.
A cousin chose a target for their righteous sabotage against tyranny.
A cousin wrote to a contact and arranged for a faction's building to fall.
A cousin chose study over sabotage, certain their work would outshine any rival.
A cousin secretly chose another family member to suffer a devastating sabotage.
An explosion tore open a wall of a cousin's estate, exposing part of their laboratory.
A nervous young messenger was caught holding a figurine that a cousin had left on the windowsill.
A cousin sent the rude messenger away and thought no more of it.
A cousin returned the signed papers to the messenger, who set off down the road.
A letter wrapped in twine appeared on the doorstep asking which flag the cousin flew.
A letter from an old university acquaintance spurred a few days of creative seclusion.
Learning who had attacked their estate, a cousin resolved to respond directly.
A cousin set the terms of a duel: scientific prowess or pistols at twenty paces.
A cousin received a letter challenging them to a duel by their own family member.
Rather than duel, a cousin issued a formal apology without admitting guilt.
A cousin accepted the duel, vowing to settle the matter with precision.
The cousins met on the dueling grounds and the shots rang out.
Neither cousin could outdo the other's science, and they left the grounds in simmering silence.
The duel ended in a fatal blow, and blood stained the dueling grounds.
The duel left the loser with a minor injury and badly wounded pride.
War had left the once handsome province scorched and ruined.
A cousin braved the last of the war to see the destroyed village with their own eyes.
A cryptic map led the cousins to an abandoned silver mine and a strange machine.

column2: A Time Machine... But, I Thought...?
column4: The cousins wondered whether they had found a way to travel through time.
Time spiralled around the machine, and a cousin wondered whether it was the Masterwork of their lineage.
The cousins emerged from the mine to find the town returned to its state in 1831.
The cousins realised that leaving past experiments unfinished could have catastrophic consequences.
A cousin felt the timestream mend and surged forward with new knowledge.
The time machine was restored to its former magnificence.
A damaged clasp on the time machine revealed schematics for devices far beyond the age.
A confused officer insisted that he knew a cousin and wanted to show them something.
The enraged officer was carried away by the police, shouting that he knew who the cousin was.
At his home the officer showed a figure identical to the one in the cousin's pocket, and snatched it away.
Watching in secret, a cousin saw the parents' hoard of knowledge, goods or money make the region famous.
Fearing the war would destroy two generations of work, the cousins looked for a more decisive solution.
Armed riflemen questioned a cousin about their allegiances and the traitorous activities in the hills.
The cousins shared their stories of the military visits and promised each other a way out if the gambit failed.
The cousins blamed one of their own, whose estate was ransacked and set ablaze by soldiers.
The cousins' bickering left the soldiers without a clear traitor, so they taxed everyone.
No cousin blamed another, and the soldiers rewarded their solidarity.
Studying the rifts in time gave a cousin a new understanding of fourth-dimensional forces.
Time went on as normal, though it was unclear whether reality had been altered.
An aged cousin stepped into the fully repaired time machine, hoping to secure the future war had taken.
With some hasty tinkering, the rusted time machine sputtered to life.
The time machine made alarming noises as a cousin pulled the lever anyway.
Under Monarchist rule, influence was gained through money and bloodshed.
The new government discovered that a family member had consorted with the enemy for over a decade.
With the royals less interested in weaponry, a cousin set out on a new path.
A cousin learned that coin and a persuasive meal could sway the royal advisor.
Direct access to royalty brought a cousin's work curious attention.
The Queen took notice of a cousin's ambitions, and the guard began watching the estate.
The crown's attention laid a cousin's secret work bare.
A cousin visited the portly royal advisor in the new Monarchist building.

column1: Reign1b Reign2b Reign3b Reign4b Reign6b Reign7b Reign7c2 Reign8b
column4: The advisor followed a cousin's suggestion for his decree and thanked them for the assistance.
The cousins discovered that their wooden figures fit together.
The cousins had to decide whether to rule with benevolence or an iron fist.
The royal advisor proposed a statue in a cousin's honour.
A cousin visited the commemorative statue of the family.
The statue's honouree was moved to tears by their monument.
A rival sneered at the statue but left reinvigorated by hate.
The Separatists celebrated their victory with a parade through the streets.

column2: The War to End All Wars
column4: The cousins' inventions spearheaded a war for the continent, and each wanted the credit.
A cousin developed aggressive new peace-keeping measures for a world war.
The Separatist government asked the family to help pay for rebuilding after the civil war.
Time had taken its toll on the family's reputation, though past contributions still helped.
A famine in 1901 caused riots, and a new meat product was proposed as a solution.
The riots ceased as mysterious new meat rations appeared and no one asked where they came from.
The people rebelled after another winter of rationing and held a grudge against the family.
A cousin found a hidden compartment in an old wooden figure.
A cousin claimed the era as their own as the fate of the world rested in their hands.
Uprisings at home diverted resources as the nation neared victory.
The cousins released a deadly gas that pacified the people at a terrible cost.
The cousins refused to use the gas, and the uprisings slowed the advance across the continent.
Raised away from their family, a cousin discovered the experiments and journals of their ancestors.
An old wooden figure seemed to bring a cousin good fortune.
An old wooden figure seemed to bring a cousin ill fortune, even after it was thrown into the fire.
The villagers welcomed a cousin's work and even opened their coffers to them.
A cousin noted that the civil war of the previous generation had ended with few details recorded.
Schematics for advanced convenience devices arrived from an unknown source.
A metal box appeared in a flash during tea, and the course of the universe shifted.
The sky glowed crimson and the air crackled as time shifted once more.
A strange premonition warned a cousin that things were about to change.
The crimson sky faded, and the cousins resolved to finish their great-grandfather's Masterwork.
Under a swirling green sky a flickering letter asked which flag the cousin flew.
A cousin became obsessed with a letter that existed in two times at once.
A letter revealed the grandparents' role in the resistance.
The time loop closed, and the timeline stabilised.
Loose ends in time caused fascinating oddities to appear.
Raised away from their family, a cousin discovered the experiments and journals of their ancestors.
Aged time travellers emerged from a metal contraption in a burst of lightning.
A dinner guest recognised a small figure on the mantle as a relic of the war.
The figure became the talk of the town and a source of intrigue for a cousin's work.
An exhibition of the family's preserved works won the admiration of academics.
A cousin set out to improve upon their great-grandfather's outdated blueprints.
An art critic believed the misshapen wooden figure was a lost work of a famous sculptor.
Inside a hollow wooden figure lay an object that could not exist.
The cousins had to choose between publishing the time machine schematics and keeping them secret.
The time machine schematics were published to the public.
The time machine schematics remained a family secret.

column2: The Consequences of Free Time Travel
column4: With time travel available to almost anyone, its random effects spread through the region.
With no monument built, the people rebuilt a landscape torn apart by time paradoxes.
The town thanked the family for setting it on the path to a Utopian future and honoured the best among them with a monument.
